title: The Legend record label and the dishonest partner
summary: He and Buddy Collette, Al Aarons and others started Legend, which fell apart when a partner dipped into the petty cash.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You were partners in a record company with Buddy...
Buddy Collette Al Aarons, Grover Mitchell, Leroy Vinnegar, Al Viola.
The name of the label?
Legend. And I won't mention... We had another partner who didn't...
Didn't work out.
Didn't work out, no.
From what I heard.
Oh, you heard all about it. Yeah, he dipped into the petty cash. So we gave that one up. Since then, Rare Records has taken over the name Legend.
Ray Avery.
Callender (#3) - 29

Ray Avery has taken that name. We thought that because of the partner that didn't do right, we had lost title to it, so it... Anyhow, Ray Avery now has the label. And he didn't do anything shady. He is one of the beautiful people also.
Right. He has taken over your catalogue or just the name?

Just the name Legend. Also, we have another label, RGB, which stands for Red, Grover and Buddy. So there are just three of us now that maintain a label. And on that label, I released Ike Isaacs' album called The Pied Piper with Jack Wilson and Jimmie Smith and Ike Isaacs, who died a couple of years ago.
The drummer Jimmie Smith.
The drummer Jimmie Smith, yeah. Thank you. I wouldn't want to make that mistake. And that's a very good album. Do you have it, by any chance?
No, I didn't even know about it.
Oh, I'll have to get that to you. It's an excellent album.
How many records did you put out under Legend when you had it? You had an album...
I had an album, Buddy had an album, Al Viola and Leroy. We had intended all of us doing albums, but then
Callender (#3) - 30

the finances got bogged down with the unsavory character we had handling business. That's what happened. I find that musicians in particular have to be able to watch their own businesses, because you trust people, and they think they're entitled to all of the spoils after you've worked for them.
